attributes.body:
In addition to 'passive' verbs, れる and られる (the auxiliary verbs) are used when expressing possibility '可能（かのう）'.

られる will be attached to the base form of る-Verbs (the form after る has been removed). Note also that れる and られる themselves behave like standard る-Verbs, so can be conjugated into a variety of different tenses in the same way as a standard verb.

A common sight in modern Japanese is words where the ら may be removed, 'ラ抜（ぬ）き言葉（ことば）', and れる may be used by itself. However, this is not technically correct Japanese, and may cause confusion in cases where ら is required (with る-Verbs and くる, when られる is expressing 'passivity', 'respect', or 'spontaneous occurrence').

For う-Verbs, they will behave a little differently. Instead of the final kana of the verb changing to an あ sound, and then adding れる (as would be the case with passive verbs), the final kana of the verb will change to an え sound (る will become れ, う will become え, す will become せ, etc.) before adding る.

Interestingly, する verbs do not have a 'potential' form, and the verb できる will be used in its place.

Caution

ことができる and られる (when used in its 'potential' meaning) have exactly the same nuance. However, many people consider ことができる to be slightly more polite.

Fun Fact

When using the potential form, either を or が may be used to mark the 'object'. You will need to be careful though, as this does not apply to できる, which may only ever use が.

attributes.source: [DBJG] A Dictionary of Basic Japanese Grammar

attributes.description: CAN /potential form（られる/ことができる）
Expressing the ability to do something

attributes.body: Passive and potential forms have different meanings but can be confusing because some forms overlap. For う-verbs, the forms are distinct. For example, 言われる 'to be said' (passive) vs. 言える means 'can say' (potential). For る-verbs, a form like 食べられる can mean either 'to be eaten' (passive) or 'can eat' (potential), and which is intended must be determined from context.

attributes.body: Both 聞こえる and 聞ける can mean 'can hear,' but differ in nuance. 聞こえる refers to a sound being audible, while 聞ける indicates the ability to hear or listen. For example, a bird chirping nearby would be 聞こえる, but being able to stream a song would be 聞ける.

first_relatable.title: 聞こえる
first_relatable.meaning: To be audible, To sound (like), (Can) hear, To be heard

attributes.body: Both 見える and 見られる mean 'can see' (potential form) but their nuances differ. 見える describes something being visible, while 見られる refers to the ability to view something. For example, stars in the sky are 見える, but being able to watch a movie on a streaming service would be 見られる.

first_relatable.title: 見える
first_relatable.meaning: To be visible, To seem, To be in sight

attributes.body: 得る・得る and the れる・られる (Potential) form both indicate possibility or ability, but differ in nuance. れる・られる is used for general ability, as in 話せる 'can speak', and is conversational. 得る is more formal and written-style, and is typically that something is possible or conceivable, like 起こり得る ('It could happen.').

Both express potential or ability, like 'can do'. ことができる is more formal and common in writing, e.g. 書くことができる 'can write', while the potential form れる・られる is shorter and used in conversation, e.g. 書ける 'can write'. The meaning is the same, but usage differs by tone and context.
